verdict.rationale: Luma's Ray page documents camera motion transfer: you can copy cinematic camera moves from a source video onto new scenes. That gives creators a first-party way to direct camera motion instead of accepting the model's choice, but only by supplying a reference clip. Multi-keyframe control governs what changes and holds, not camera paths, so it is not credited here. missing for 10: explicit named camera controls (pan, zoom, orbit, static) without a source video, documentation of how camera direction works in text- or image-to-video, independent or hands-on corroboration of camera-move control.

support.subject: As a creator, I can direct camera moves (pan, zoom, orbit, static) instead of accepting whatever motion the model picks

citations.quote: Transfer cinematic camera moves across scenes, worlds, and styles.
Apply motion from a source video to new subjects, scenes, or styles.
